text: Fez is an Anti-game game.  It is a puzzle instead.  The platforming, jumping, and maneuvering are all for one purpose - to get to the puzzles that need to be solved in the new game + mode. It looks like a 2.5d platformer, but in the end, there are ciphers, obtuse observation puzzles, and QR codes that need to be solved.  The are difficult, and require patience and relaxed time. A game to be played while drinking a glass of red wine or port, and relaxing by the warm fire of your computer's processor while your brain slowly bakes in the overheated bytes. A rating?  A great game, but not...for...everyone.

text: Probably one of the best games I've ever played. It's very relaxed while still being engaging, with puzzles that you can pop in to, try to solve, give up on and come back to. Yet the satisfaction of actually solving a puzzle, or completing a cube, is immense. It helps that the game is beautiful, with great music and a lovely atmosphere. Plus, the whole perspective thing is really fun, clever and eye-opening. In the least pretentious way possible. I should probably add that I have by no means completed FEZ, and I'm unlikely to. As amazing as the puzzles are, I don't really have the energy to make notes of three (?) different languages and use them to solve the more difficult puzzles. But I think this game has enough content besides that to make it worth it, so I'd really just say the more complicated stuff that requires more dedication is an added bonus.

text: In all honesty, this game can be either one of two things, a time killer or a game to play with friends.  When it comes to being a scary game, it is effective the first few times but you'll get used to the games tricks very quickly.  Yeah, that is pretty much what there is to say.  And yes, it is true, there are quite a bit of fans who like to praise this game as "the best game ever" but as long as you know what the game is trying to accomplish (which is to help you kill some time in small game with a interesting story), you can bypass all of that If you are gamer who is into a game for outstanding gameplay with an extensive area to explore then skip this game or wait until you can play with a friend. If you are thinking about the game for a scary experience then I would wait for a sale or a price drop.  As mentioned before, once you seen all the tricks once...they don't have the same shock value as before.  Though the game may still hold your interest if you are into dark humor If you are into a game for its extensive lore, fandom, and story line then...let's face it, you already bought the whole series.

text: This game is truly amazing. I am a FNaF enthusiast, I know most of the massive story behind it, and I love every bit of it. But, I only had played FnaF 2 on my mobile, which was awesome! (I beat 9/10 custom nights) So I decidded to get the classic FNaF for my PC. But man, is this game HARD. I breezed through nights 1-4, and it took me a few tries to finish night 5. But night 6 took me a whopping 29 tries. around 22 of those tries I died because of Freddy playing his short jingle in the power out. Overall, this is uniquely designed, and very frustrating, though in the end it is all worth it. 100/100 for the classic indie horror game, and I highly recommend this for whoever is looking for a serious challenge (20/20/20/20 mode is near impossible, but doable), fright, and an overall exciting and fun game!

title: five nights at freddy's
text: Nothing ruins something more than an onslaught of ridiculously obssessive fans that like to bang on about something, because a part of your interest in a game is automatically jaded from the large likelihood of a game not being as brilliant as they want to tell you. No, don't get me wrong. In its entirety, Five Nights at Freddy's is pretty good. But because of the 12 year olds that haven't heard of four simple words, "Resident Evil" and "Silent Hill", the Five Nights at Freddy's game has turned from being a potentially brilliant series into nothing more than a mainstream fad. Once FNAF 4 comes, and give it a few months, and I guarantee this series will be banished into the abyss of obscurity. It happened to Amnesia, it happened to Slender. It's the hard truth of the mainstream gaming community. But I digress. When Five Nights at Freddy's does something well, it does something, reeeeallly well. It's not "just jumpscares". Heck, the only jumpscares that happens is when you die. What this game excels at is tension. The lack of movement and vision allows your paranoid imaginations to run free and plays you into the hands of the animatronics. The almost silent room, with the exception of the fan that's draining your energy like the AAA gaming developers drain my soul, is crippling, and really allows you to sink everything in, the fact that you only have one shot to keep Freddy, Foxy, Chica, and Bonnie away from you or your done for. Somehow, practically all of the elements of this game combine to somehow work, despite pre-rendered animations, simple gameplay, and stock children cheering sound effects. Is Five Nights at Freddy's talked about to death? Absolutely, but Scott's not to blame for that. I'm here to play what Scott has presented, not play what the fanboys have presented; and what Scott has presented is the first horror game to get to me in a long long long time, and that's not just a theory. 8.5/10
